markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (82%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Invasive · Careful review

InSitu stays in the 90% conformal set, and this is a stain-degraded simulated frozen section. [F1]

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 82%, InSitu 18% | Clear lead, not decisive |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive | Two classes not separable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / percentile 1.0 | Not flagged; stain degraded |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Invasive | Mixed neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (regions 1, 5, 9) · ↑ invasive · Largest concept association in this case [F2] · Unreliable
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 1, 5) · ↑ invasive · Second-largest invasive association [F3] · Unreliable
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 2, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Points toward in situ rather than invasive [F4] · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Very small invasive association · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 1, 5) · ↑ invasive · Small invasive association · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses and necrosis are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Stain degradation inflates mitosis and necrosis scores, both of which failed spot checks.
- Intraductal in situ disease is present; InSitu is in the conformal set.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 2, 6, 10:** Check whether atypical cells stay within intact ducts.
2. **Regions 1, 5, 9:** Confirm true mitoses and necrosis versus stain artifact.
3. **Regions 4, 8:** Confirm tumor at the medial cut edge. [F7]
